To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presynaptic particle fraction (PPF) is enriched with clathrin‐coated vesicle proteins, and the postsynaptic density fraction (PSD) is enriched with proteins of the actin‐associated cytoskeleton.

(a) the presynaptic particle fraction is composed of presynaptic components, (b) the presynptic particle fraction is insoluble in pH 6.5 buffered TX‐100, (c) the presynctic particle fraction is soluble in pH 8.5 buffered TX100 and (d) clathrin might anchor many proteins in the presynptic compartment.

the presynaptic particle fraction is insoluble to TX‐100 at pH 6 but soluble at pH 8, contains proteins that are concentrated in presynaptic specialisations, and is composed of a large number of proteins that are not connected to actin‐based structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie synaptic transmission.
the structure and composition of the postsynaptic density (PSD) of the central synapse.
the identification of the proteins in the postsynaptic densities and presynaptic particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has shown that the PPF contains a large number of proteins that are involved in vesicle trafficking and that these proteins can be solubilized in a pH 8.5 detergent extraction, but not in a pH 6 extraction, and that this solubility difference is due to a pH‐dependent change in clathrin conformation.

the PSD‐PPF complex is an important part of the transsynaptic specialization and that its components, including clathrin and actin, are involved in the formation of the synaptic vesicle pool and in the synaptic transmission process.

the PPF fraction consists of proteins that are concentrated in the synaptic vesicle fraction, but not connected with the actin‐cytoskeleton, and are insoluble in detergent at pH6.0 but soluble in pH8.0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the presynaptic particle fraction is composed of a large number of proteins that are not associated with the actin‐cytoskeletal framework.
presynaptic proteins are not connected to actin and that clathrin could be a scaffold for many proteins of the presynapse.

the presynaptic scaffold is a highly organized network of proteins, including clathrin and actin‐binding proteins, that is anchored to the presynaptic plasma membrane and is connected with postsynaptic densities via the actin‐binding protein spectrin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a large difference between the proteome of postsynaptic densities and that of the presynapse.
the PPF contains a large number of proteins not previously known to be associated with the presynaptic terminal.
we have identified a novel presynaptic fraction that contains proteins that are involved in the synaptic vesicle cycle.
